_readme: Hand-authored structures for the molecules of one patent that resolve_structures.py
cannot get any other way. One entry per MOLECULE, keyed by an exact identifier string
from gold/compounds.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: 0 of the 75 compound records carry smiles, inchi or
molecular_formula, and gold/structures.json only covers what the patent DRAWS. Every
reagent that is named but never drawn (methanesulfonyl chloride, thionyl chloride,
triethylamine and the rest) has no structure anywhere in the pipeline, and half of them
carry a mass/mole pair that the downstream mass-balance check cannot use without a
formula. Those are the entries below.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE: spelling variants. The pipeline already knows that
'2-chloro-6-(methanesulfonyl)toluene' and '2-chloro-6-(methylsulfonyl)toluene' are one
molecule, because finalise.py wrote that out to provenance/compounds-equivalence.json.
resolve_structures.py propagates a structure across each equivalence group and tags the
copies origin 'derived'. Write one entry, for one spelling, and let it propagate. The
optional 'aliases' list is only for synonyms the equivalence index misses, such as
'anhydrous aluminium trichloride' against 'aluminium trichloride'.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE EITHER: molecules the patent draws. Those come out of
gold/structures.json with origin 'patent_drawing', which is a stronger provenance claim
than 'curated'. An entry here for a drawn molecule is harmless (the join is on RDKit
canonical SMILES, so it lands on the same molecule and keeps the stronger origin) but it
is work you did not need to do.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: 'cyclohexanedione' (Claims). The gold records it resolved:false
because the patent prints it with no ring locants, so which isomer is meant is not
stated. Supplying the 1,3-dione here would silently resolve what the annotator
deliberately left open. It gets origin 'none'. Same for the unresolved Chinese class
terms, and for water, HCl, MgSO4 and the other trivial reagents, which carry no
chemistry and are noise when drawn.
FIELDS: 'smiles' is required and must parse in RDKit. 'slug' is optional and names the
SVG file; omit it and one is derived from the identifier. 'aliases' and 'note' are
optional. formula, mw and canonical are NOT stored here: resolve_structures.py computes
them with RDKit on every run and writes them into gold/structures-resolved.json, so
there is one place they can be wrong instead of two.
Every SMILES below was checked atom by atom against its IUPAC name before it was
committed. A wrong structure here silently corrupts a mass-balance check downstream.

2-chlorotoluene.note: Starting material of the prose route (Example 1 step 1). Not drawn in the patent: the drawn scheme starts from 2,6-dichlorotoluene instead.

methanesulfonyl chloride.note: Sulfonylating agent, step 1. Supplies the methylsulfonyl group of every downstream intermediate.

aluminium trichloride.note: Friedel-Crafts catalyst, charged in steps 1 and 2. Written as three covalent Al-Cl bonds so RDKit gives the AlCl3 formula weight; the real solid is dimeric and this depiction is a formula, not a structure claim.

2-chloro-6-(methylsulfonyl)toluene.note: Route step 1 product. Drawn in the patent. C8H9ClO2S = 204.68; the printed 34.0 g / 200 mmol implies 170.0, which is the des-chloro analogue (AUDIT p07).

2-chloro-3-acetyl-6-(methylsulfonyl)tolu.note: Route step 2 product. Drawn in the patent, and drawn a second time on p07 under the toluene-based name while p06 names the same structure as an ethan-1-one.

2-chloro-3-methyl-4-(methylsulfonyl)benz.note: Route step 3 product, from haloform oxidation of the aryl methyl ketone. Drawn in the patent.

methyl 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-(methylsulfon.note: Route step 4 product. Drawn in the patent.

bromine.note: Benzylic brominating agent, step 5, replacing the NBS of the prior art. Br2 = 159.81; the printed 39.6 g / 220 mmol implies 180.0, i.e. OVER by 20.2.

methyl 2-chloro-3-(bromomethyl)-4-(methy.note: Route step 5 product. Drawn in the patent. The p06 read names it 'methyl 3-(bromomethyl)-2-chloro-4-...' and the p08 read 'methyl 3-(bromomethyl)-2-chloro-4-(methanesulfonyl)...'; neither string equals this record name, which is why the join is on canonical SMILES.

sodium 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxide.note: Supplies the 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy group in step 6. Written as the separated ion pair, which is what the mass/mole pair is computed against.

sodium hydroxide.note: Saponifies the methyl ester in step 6. Present only because it carries a mass/mole pair that the MW check has to be able to compute.

2-chloro-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methy.note: Route step 6 product. Drawn in the patent.

thionyl chloride.note: Converts the acid to the acid chloride in step 7.

cyclohexane-1,3-dione.note: Supplies the dione ring in step 7. NOT aliased to the Claims record 'cyclohexanedione': that record is resolved:false because the patent prints no ring locants there, and resolving it here would erase a real finding.

triethylamine.note: Acid scavenger in steps 7 and 8. Carries a mass/mole pair in both.

3-oxo-1-cyclohexen-1-yl 2-chloro-3-[(2,2.note: Route step 7 product, the O-acyl enol ester. Drawn in the patent. C17H16ClF3O6S = 440.82, the SAME formula as tembotrione because step 8 is a Fries-type rearrangement; the printed 198.0 g / 500 mmol implies 396.0 (AUDIT p09).

tembotrione.note: The target. Route step 8 product, the C-acyl 1,3-dione from rearrangement of the step 7 enol ester. Drawn in the patent twice (p06 scheme step 9 and p09). The gold record carries this same SMILES as an alias.

ethyl 2-chloro-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy.note: Ethyl ester variant named in the claims. Never drawn, and never charged with a mass, so it exists here only so the claims text renders with a structure.

Cc1c(Cl)cccc1Cl.note: 2,6-dichlorotoluene. The gold record carries this SMILES AS its identifier (identifier_type smiles), so it resolves as patent_scheme. It is the starting material of the DRAWN scheme, which is a different route from the prose: the prose starts from 2-chlorotoluene. All 9 drawn records carry validation_flag route_attribution_unclear.

CSc1cccc(Cl)c1C.note: 2-chloro-6-(methylsulfanyl)toluene. Product of drawn scheme step 1 (CH3SNa). The thioether entry the prose explicitly says the invention does away with, so it has no prose counterpart.

CSc1ccc(C(C)=O)c(Cl)c1C.note: Product of drawn scheme step 2. Oxidised to the sulfone at scheme step 3, which is where the drawn route rejoins the prose route.

cyanoacetone.note: 3-oxobutanenitrile. Named as the step 8 additive by all three written tellings of the route, and the compound [0004] says the invention eliminated, calling it highly toxic. Curated because the patent never draws it. IT IS ONE HALF OF THE PAIR A REVIEWER IS ASKED TO TELL APART: claims CN104292137A_p02_x3 and CN104292137A_p05_x3 ask whether step 8 means this or acetone cyanohydrin, which the drawn scheme shows instead. The two are distinguishable by name only to a chemist, and trivially by eye once both are drawn: this one is a straight three-carbon chain carrying a ketone, the other is branched at a quaternary carbon carrying an OH. The entry exists so the reviewer can settle the question by looking rather than by trusting a name.

acetone cyanohydrin.note: 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile. What the drawn scheme shows above the step 8 arrow, drawn as a structure rather than written: a quaternary carbon bearing CN, OH and two methyls. Curated because it is drawn but never named in the text, so gold/structures.json does not carry it under this identifier. THE OTHER HALF OF THE PAIR: see the note on cyanoacetone. Drawing both is the whole point, because the comparison is the evidence and neither drawing settles the question on its own.
